9e98d507 (condensed into ae22657) is explicitly unfinished and must not be merged as-is.

Required work Evidence
Integrate the allocation-error patch. It exists only as a patch file. 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:85-116 (condensed into ae22657); handoff/memory-error.patch
Integrate and finish ordered pullback reductions. Current production callers still use nondeterministic Rayon reductions. 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:118-142 (condensed into ae22657); crates/treams-core/src/numerics/parallel.rs:117-165
Resolve the known Clippy failure and failing reproducibility test. 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:156-168 (condensed into ae22657); tests/bindings/test_thread_pool.py:155-166
Reconcile unsupported release claims. Public docs already promise bit-identical gradients and allocation failures becoming MemoryError. 9e98d507:python/treams_rs/parallel.py:23-24 (condensed into ae22657); docs/design/parallelism.md:113-123
Regenerate documentation and remove obsolete caveats after implementation. 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:169-189,268-270 (condensed into ae22657)
Delete handoff/ after recovering its changes and useful evidence. Embedded patches currently also violate whitespace hygiene. 9e98d507:handoff/README.md:3-5,173-174 (condensed into ae22657)

The allocation patch needs a precise scope decision. It converts selected large outputs and LU workspaces, but still leaves infallible allocations in matrix products, SVD/eigenvalue workspaces, periodic expansion tables, and binding input copies (handoff/README.md:113-116). For example, crates/treams-py/src/convert.rs:305-314 still duplicates potentially large arrays with infallible allocations. Either finish the consequential large-allocation paths or narrow public guarantees to the implemented coverage. The patch’s Linux subprocess tests cover two refused requests, not every allocation path.

Ordered reductions require memory validation as well as numerical tests. try_fold_ordered retains as many as 64 complete partial gradients before combining them (crates/treams-core/src/numerics/parallel.rs:120,154-159). The plane-field patch improves this by partitioning the longer axis into up to 32 blocks, but its new formulas and allocation patterns still need the full Python derivative suite and representative peak-RSS checks (handoff/ordered-reductions-wip.patch:1296-1364).

The existing handoff reports both patches together passed formatting, Clippy and 235 Rust tests; these are historical assertions, not checks rerun here. It explicitly leaves Python tests, generated docs and wheel checks unrun (handoff/README.md:144-154). Proposed validation after reconciliation:

  • Build a fresh extension; run just ci, regenerate docs, and run just check-wheel.
  • Exercise the Python suite with one thread and multiple threads, including every pullback case in tests/bindings/test_thread_pool.py.
  • Run fork, forkserver and spawn tests after prior native work, budget/context restoration, threadpoolctl, ufunc reductions/accumulation, and floating-environment checks.
  • Run the allocation subprocess tests; add coverage for any newly converted large-allocation paths.
  • Measure memory for representative large field and cluster pullbacks; qualify Linux/macOS and x86-64/ARM support at the release artifact boundary.

Source overlap is limited but needs deliberate reconciliation: newer improvements changes overlap this branch in CHANGELOG.md and tests/api/test_namespaces.py; framework changes overlap in CHANGELOG.md and docs/development/benchmarks.md. The two embedded patches overlap in fields.rs imports, with the intended resolution recorded at handoff/README.md:146-149. No merge simulation was performed.

The remaining open-work table (docs/design/parallelism.md:125-139) mixes release qualification with optional optimization. Deterministic parallel SVD, smarter parallel cutoffs, LU scheduling calibration, reduced ufunc copying, faster assembly, and translation-plan optimization can remain deferred. Retain the current sequential decompositions and GIL-enabled configuration unless those optimizations are explicitly selected. Interruptibility and typed panic behavior require an explicit documented release boundary.

I found no additional high-confidence mathematical defect beyond these acknowledged unfinished paths. This was source-only inspection; no edits, checkouts, builds, tests, commits, pushes or remote changes were made.
